# Project Aham by BoredMutant

> Project Aham is an early-stage, WhatsApp-first service transaction network being built by BoredMutant. It is intended to connect consumer requests with participating businesses whose centrally managed agents can return structured offers and coordinate bookings. The initial operational focus is Hyderabad, India.

Canonical URL: https://www.boredmutant.com/
Project: https://github.com/Chief-1901/Boredmutant
Conversation: https://cal.com/boredmutant/automations

## Product direction

- Consumers describe a real-world service need in WhatsApp, including relevant location, timing and budget constraints.
- A central orchestrator is designed to find eligible participating businesses and ask their agents for current availability and structured offers.
- Offers should state scope, price, timing, terms and expiry. Consumers compare offers and authorize actions according to their preferences and time-bounded mandates.
- A booking is reported as confirmed only after the provider's authoritative booking path confirms it and the result is recorded.
- Businesses are intended to configure services, availability, pricing and escalation rules. Onboarding may begin conversationally, but WhatsApp, calendar or booking connections can require a secure provider handoff or browser-based authorization.

## Safety and transaction rules

- LLMs may interpret requests, ask clarifying questions, summarize offers and draft communication.
- Deterministic application rules govern authorization, transaction state and side effects. A model cannot approve spending, fabricate availability or confirm a booking.
- Ambiguous, unsupported or out-of-policy cases should be declined or escalated to a person.
- A2A is the primary agent interoperability direction; UCP compatibility is intended where capabilities match, with MCP and REST for tools and integrations.

## Current implementation

- The repository has a Fastify API, separate worker process, shared Zod schemas, transaction and policy primitives, and PostgreSQL migrations for the planned production data model.
- A deterministic local demo uses Node's built-in SQLite support and mock offers/bookings. It is not a production booking service.
- A WhatsApp Cloud API adapter and webhook routes are present. The current local inbound flow calls no LLM; it is restricted to the configured demo phone.
- Live customer transactions, verified business onboarding, production provider integrations and production use of PostgreSQL remain future work. The project is not production-ready.

## Initial scope and limits

The first planned transaction patterns are fixed-price appointments, quote-required services and consultations. Hyderabad is the first operational market, while the architecture is intended to support additional geographies and service categories after validation.

Healthcare is limited to administrative appointment handling only after privacy, consent, provider verification and operational review. No diagnosis, triage or medical advice. The initial release does not include arbitrary outreach to non-member businesses, holding customer funds, or unreviewed payment processing.
